description: Article 19 has documented at least 174 murders and 31 disappearances of journalists in Mexico since 2000. Counts differ by methodology - Article 19 listed 157 killings 2000-2022 while the Atlantic Council's count gave 163.
energy_note: A hundred and seventy-four, and counting.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the worst year, and the ranking
description: 2022 was the deadliest year, with 13 killings per CPJ and Article 19 - the Atlantic Council counted 18. RSF ranked Mexico the deadliest country for the press three consecutive years, and second worldwide in 2025 with at least nine killed.
energy_note: Worst in the world, three years running.

aspect: EXAMPLE - most attacks are by officials, not cartels
description: Contrary to the cartel-centric assumption, Article 19 found 42% of attacks on the press are committed by government officials, ahead of criminal actors and private entities. In 2022 Mexico recorded an attack on journalists or media houses every 13 hours.
energy_note: The state is the single largest attacker.

description: All but a handful of killings and abductions of media workers remain unsolved. Veracruz is the deadliest state.
energy_note: Almost none of them are ever solved.
